note: Triennial election of the Dungannon rural district councillors, 1930. Mr. Wm. M'Guffin, returning officer, received one nomination for each of the nineteen divisions (Irish News, 24 April 1930, p. 5); there were no opposed returns in Dungannon (Belfast News-Letter, 25 April 1930, p. 8). No poll was held; Tyrone's polling day was Wednesday 4 June 1930. Printed 'Beragh' (the Bernagh division). Returned unopposed.
correctionNote: Renamed from 'Beragh' to Bernagh (13 Nov 2026, by the owner's rule for division spellings: the official or DED-map name where there is one, otherwise the spelling most rounds use): the 1948 order naming Dungannon Rural District's nineteen divisions (Ministry of Health and Local Government, 26 August 1948; Belfast Gazette, 1 April 1949) and the DED maps of 1921-69 (BERNAGH; Beragh is a division of Omagh Rural) spell it Bernagh. This round was filed under the spelling 'Beragh', a form of the division's name it keeps as an alias; the old address (beragh) answers with a redirect to this one.
